title: Integral completion unit and its normalized partial transpose
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and a scheme $W$ on which $\ell$ is invertible. Use the derived category of modules over the completed integral coefficient sheaf [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], its ordinary tensor and derived reduction/limit adjunction with the normalized reduction-tensor and Roos comparisons [def-pur-completed-pullback-tensor-comparison], and the completed tensor [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. Define the ordinary-to-completed tensor unit $u_{M,N}:M\otimes^L N\to M\widehat\otimes^L N$ to be the ordinary reduction/limit adjunction unit at $M\otimes^L N$, followed by the derived limit of the reduction-tensor comparison and the inverse Roos tensor realization. On the bounded constructible derived-complete category [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] with completed tensor and the permitted internal-Hom pairs of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], define the partial closed structure [def-pod-partial-closed-interfaces] to be the uniquely normalized one whose transpose of every map $b:L\widehat\otimes^L M\to N$ is the ordinary closed transpose of $u_{L,M}$ followed by $b$, viewed through the full-subcategory inclusions. Thus the structure includes all additive Hom equivalences and their naturality, with no perfectness restriction beyond the recorded Hom-pair domain. This definition uses the published uniqueness characterization of the partial closed structure, not an arbitrary choice of a map.
